class_name: 同時性-対比-タトオモウト類

provenance.pipeline: satsuki v1 (v1.0.1 editorial re-edit: usage-note reshaping corpus-wide, lane discrimination for same-surface families, against prompts/style.md)

patterns.usage_note: Reports two events as effectively instantaneous with the speaker's surprise built in: attached to the plain past, the second half is unexpected or the flat opposite of what the first half promised (席に着いたかと思うと、もう眠っていた). It describes something witnessed, so it is typically not used of the speaker's own actions, and the second clause states what happened rather than a request, command, or intention.

examples.ruby: 弟[おとうと]は席[せき]に着[つ]いたかと思[おも]うと、もう眠[ねむ]っていた。
examples.english: My brother had barely sat down before he was fast asleep.

examples.ruby: 太陽[たいよう]が沈[しず]んだかと思[おも]うと、辺[あた]りは真[ま]っ暗[くら]になった。
examples.english: No sooner had the sun gone down than everything around us went pitch black.

examples.ruby: 妹[いもうと]は家[いえ]に入[はい]ってきたかと思[おも]うと、もう出[で]かけて行[い]った。
examples.english: My sister walked in the door and was straight back out again.

patterns.usage_note: Says the second event followed hard on the first, allowing a real if short gap and carrying no surprise (列車が駅を出ると間もなく、車掌が切符を見に来た). It attaches to the dictionary form, unlike the past-form siblings 〜たかと思うと and 〜たかと思う間もなく, which report no gap at all. Being a と clause, the second half reports an observed outcome, never a request, invitation, or command, where 〜てから and 〜たあとで take those freely.

examples.ruby: 列車[れっしゃ]が駅[えき]を出[で]ると間[ま]もなく、車掌[しゃしょう]が切符[きっぷ]を見[み]に来[き]た。
examples.english: Shortly after the train pulled out of the station, the conductor came around to check tickets.

examples.ruby: カップ麺[めん]に湯[ゆ]を注[そそ]ぐと間[ま]もなく、狭[せま]い部屋[へや]にだしの香[かお]りが満[み]ちた。
examples.english: Not long after I poured the water into the cup noodles, the smell of broth filled the little room.

examples.ruby: 予約[よやく]すると間[ま]もなく、確認[かくにん]のメールが届[とど]いた。
examples.english: A confirmation email arrived not long after I made the booking.

patterns.canonical_surface: だかとおもうまもなく
glosses: with no time even to register …
patterns.usage_note: Removes even the sliver of a gap that 〜たかと思うと tolerates: the second event lands on top of the first with no interval (地面が揺れたかと思う間もなく、天井が崩れ落ちた). The sibling 〜と間もなく reports an ordinary short interval instead. Narration rather than conversation, at home with disasters and accidents, and it often follows a quoted thought as well as a plain past verb (「しまった」と思う間もなく).

examples.ruby: 地面[じめん]が揺[ゆ]れたかと思[おも]う間[ま]もなく、天井[てんじょう]が崩[くず]れ落[お]ちた。
examples.english: The ground shook, and before it could even register, the ceiling came down.

examples.ruby: 自転車[じてんしゃ]が滑[すべ]ったかと思[おも]う間[ま]もなく、私[わたし]は路上[ろじょう]に投[な]げ出[だ]されていた。
examples.english: The bike slid out from under me, and before that could even register I was sprawled on the road.

examples.ruby: 波[なみ]が引[ひ]いたかと思[おも]う間[ま]もなく、次[つぎ]の高波[たかなみ]が押[お]し寄[よ]せた。
examples.english: The wave had barely drawn back before the next swell came crashing in.
